findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is undefined, null, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and this throws a TypeError whenever location equals MeetLocationType, breaking booking creation for users without a destination calendar.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination by the external id they are matching against
findings.body: In updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against externalCalendarId, which is null/empty in the fallback branch, so it never matches a meaningful calendar. The calendarId silently becomes undefined and the Google call goes to a wrong/default calendar instead of the booking's calendar.

findings.title: Reschedule/update flows lose the destination-calendar-to-credential mapping
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents now iterates every destination calendar and, for those with a credentialId, passes destination.externalId into createEvent. Meanwhile CalendarManager.createEvent sets externalId and credentialId on results, but in the non-credentialId branch the calendar is created without externalId, so the booking reference gets no externalCalendarId. Later updates/deletes then fall back to default calendars, which can orphan or duplicate events.

findings.title: Collective event pushes host calendars into the array that is later persisted to DB
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` mutates the array built from the organizer calendar. When the organizer has no destination calendar, the array is null so the push is skipped, and the non-collective fallback is inconsistent. The final `destinationCalendar: { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } }` now depends on array order, so the organizer's calendar is only preserved if it is first; other changes can silently attach the wrong calendar to the booking.

findings.title: teamDestinationCalendars is populated inside an async map and only used later
findings.body: The push into teamDestinationCalendars happens inside the async callback of users.slice(1).map, and the callback runs during map invocation, so ordering is nondeterministic relative to `await Promise.all`. More importantly, the destination calendar of each team member is pushed without checking for duplicates, so the same calendar can be added multiple times when a user is both listed in hosts and attendees.

findings.title: Team member attendee object gains firstName/lastName fields and email default changes
findings.body: The teamMemberPromises mapping adds `firstName: ""` and `lastName: ""` and changes `email` from `user.email || ""` to `user.email ?? ""`, altering the team member data passed to emails and calendar events. Empty strings are not equivalent to the previous `||` fallback for null-like values, and these unrelated changes are not described in the PR.

findings.title: loadUsers swallows dynamic-user errors and changes fallback semantics
findings.body: loadUsers now throws when dynamicUserList is empty and converts all other errors to HttpError 500 'Unable to load users'. Previously an empty dynamic list just produced no users. Also `return users.length ? users : eventType.users` changes behavior when hosts are empty. These behavior changes are unrelated to the collective destination calendar fix and can break dynamic group bookings.

findings.title: Unrelated user-visible string change
findings.body: The additionalNotes text was changed from 'organiser' to 'organizer' in createEvent. This is an unrelated text change that alters emitted notes content for existing users and is not part of the stated fix.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent signature now requires credentialId for all implementations
findings.body: Making credentialId a required parameter on the Calendar interface breaks all calendar implementations and callers not updated here (e.g. third-party or other apps calling createEvent with one argument). Type checking will pass only if every implementation was updated; the change should be justified or made optional.

findings.title: Lark createEvent ignores the credential and uses first destination calendar
findings.body: Lark's createEvent takes the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is creating the event, so with multiple destination calendars across credentials, each Lark call uses the same calendar id and events are not created on the calendar each host expects.
